outlook.statement: Indian newspaper offset printing machine industry expected to see continued demand in 2025-26 driven by need for high-volume, cost-effective printing solutions, particularly for regional and localized news. Demand for localized print media in South Asia including India expected to remain strong. Government institutions and educational bodies rely on offset printing for public bulletins, examination papers, and other materials.
The Company is continuously exploring the possibilities of exporting more of its products to countries mainly in Africa, South East Asia, Russia and Japan.

Future plans in view of Energy Conservation: Installation of ON GRID Solar power generation plant; Replacement of high power consuming conventional High Bay Metal Halide Luminaries with energy efficient LED High Bay Luminaries.

Opportunities for web offset printing machine manufacturers in India are pivoting toward education and book printing. Despite digital media growth, regional language publishing and high-volume packaging offer robust demand.
Indian education sector continues to rely heavily on printed textbooks. Government drives for mass literacy and regional language textbooks are fueling continuous, high-volume orders for publishers.
Major revenue stream involves servicing the massive installed base of existing printing presses across India through retrofits and refurbished equipment.

Global web offset printing press market projected to grow at 3.8% CAGR, but growth is uneven with declining western markets and transforming domestic/emerging markets. Indian manufacturers shifting focus from newspapers to government education contracts for printing state school textbooks and national exam curriculum guides, where web offset presses are more economical than sheet-fed or digital options.

Credit risk: The Company's activities expose it to credit risk from receivables from customers. Managed through credit approvals, establishing credit limits and continuously monitoring creditworthiness. International transactions backed by Letters of credit where necessary.
Liquidity risk: The Company has exposure to liquidity risk arising from financial instruments.
Market risk: The Company has exposure to market risk arising from financial instruments.
Actuarial risk: Gratuity plan exposed to adverse salary growth experience, variability in mortality rates, variability in withdrawal rates.
Investment risk: For funded plans relying on insurers, value of assets certified by insurer may not be fair value of instruments backing liability.
Liquidity risk (gratuity): Employees with high salaries and long durations accumulate significant benefits; resignations/retirements can strain cashflows.
Market risk (gratuity): Discount rate changes affect defined benefit obligation; valuation exposed to fluctuations in corporate/government bond yields.
Legislative risk: Government may amend Payment of Gratuity Act requiring higher benefits, directly affecting defined benefit obligation.
Credit risk from trade receivables
Liquidity risk with negative working capital
Market risk including foreign exchange rate risk (USD, EUR, JPY) and interest rate risk
Currency risk from fluctuations in USD and EUR against functional currency
No hedging of foreign exchange and interest rate exposure using derivative financial instruments
